Effects of Estrogen: The high level of estrogen at the end of the follicular phase produces a positive feedback on the brain that produces a surge of Luteinizing Hormone (LH) and a smaller amount of the Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH), which allows for the release of the rupture of the dominant follicle.
Effects of Progesterone: The levels of progesterone is low.
Effects of FSH: There is a surge of the Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH) caused by a high amount of estrogen. This surge is minor compared to the surge in the Luteinizing hormone (LH), which is the main trigger for ovulation.
Effects of LH: The high amount of estrogen produces a positive feedback that triggers a sharp peak in the amount of the Luteinizing hormone (LH). It triggers ovulation : the dominant follicle, the oocyte is released from the ovary into the fallopian tube.
Energy Levels Info: At ovulation you will be at the peak of your energy levels. This is the perfect time for endurance based exercises and participating in competitive sports.
What to eat: The best type of food to eat during ovulation are foods with high fiber and antioxidants to support ovulation and reproductive health. Foods with high protein levels are also recommended as they will be beneficial for high intensity workouts. Some examples include vegetables, berries and nuts and whole grains, such as brown rice or quinoa.
Foods and Recipes: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here.  https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration: At ovulation the concentration levels will be very high, attention and memory will be performed better and processing speed will be good. This is the best time to study and do active recall.
Health: Ovulation will always be 12-24 hours, and this will not vary the cycle length. Some people may experience pain during ovulation, however this pain can be caused by different medical conditions. If you are concerned, it is best to contact your doctor.
Mood: You will feel at your best, you will be the most outgoing and social and emotionally resilient. However depending per individual the change in hormones might result in sensitivity or moodswings, or anxiety.
Types of Vitamins: During ovulation the best vitamins and supplements to take consist of Vitamin B, antioxidants and proteins. Vitamin B will help with the cell production, antioxidants will help protect healthy cells, while proteins will support muscle recovery.
Insights in the Brain: The high amount of estrogen creates a positive feedback that stimulates the anterior pituitary to produce a the Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge and a smaller the Follicular Stimulating hormone (FSH) surge.
Insights in the Ovaries: There is a rupture of the dominant follicle, the oocyte is released into the Fallopian tube, and the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum.
Insights in the Uterus: The uterus is prepared for a possible implantation.
Phase Info: A Luteinizing hormone (LH) surge triggers ovulation : the oocyte is released into the Fallopian tube and transitions into the corpus luteum.
Today's Recap: Today you may feel a peak of energy. You might feel more attentive and have better memory, and will be more social and resilient.
